question: Do cancellation request and verification errors promptly publish conservative release receipts, retaining intervals only when shared XSync completed?
H: Any exception during cancellation release must publish one owner_release interruption marked verified=false and wake release monitoring. If XSync did not complete, no per-key interval is valid; if only post-sync keymap verification fails, completed intervals remain valid. The V13 adapter classifies both as input_release_unverified without granting authority. A later cleanup retry may independently verify release.
T: Fake-Xlib owner-thread fault injection in two phases: admit W and A, cancel, make the A KeyRelease clear fake state then raise before XSync, then separately complete XSync and make query_keymap raise. Queue an owner input_state read after cleanup, inspect receipts before close, and characterize later cleanup.

D.FAIL: Before repair, cancellation produces no owner_release receipt/interruption before close.
D.PASS: After repair, both injected exception phases record and publish unverified cancellation receipts; no-XSync intervals are empty, post-XSync intervals remain bounded, V13 grants no authority, and close later records separate verified cleanup.
D.HOLD: Fake owner cannot process the deterministic fault or the capture harness fails.

C: A reported client-side XTest error may follow server acceptance; immediate physical state in the fake backend is not authoritative. The owner must keep the failed state conservative and can still recover on a later cleanup call.
U: Fake Xlib only. No real X server, operating-system input, GUI/game effect, model, live lane, or application recovery was exercised.
red_outcome: exit 1: failed cancellation must publish one unverified owner_release
green_outcome: exit 0: unverified interruption precedes independently verified shutdown cleanup
